clue.text: Held back but given another helping

definitions.meaning: kept aside for later use, like a table booked in advance
served again, a second portion at the table, read as RE- plus served

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RE (again) plus SERVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in hand or booked ahead is withheld; and dished up a second time is served once more.

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction with salesman over the fish

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A diner complains to the salesman about the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only works in a down clue: the salesman is written above the fish in the grid. A roach is a common European river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or criticise someone for a fault, to blame them.

clue.text: Moving suddenly, outside left is unexpected

indicators.note: outside means the word for moving suddenly goes round the letter for left

parts.note: starting means jumping or moving suddenly in surprise

explanation.surface: An outside-left winger darting off suddenly catches everyone by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside left' looks like a football position, but 'outside' puts STARTING round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprising and alarming; both words describe something that catches one off guard.

clue.text: Quickly improvise in game, coming up with a quip

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up means the word for quip reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pun is a quip or play on words

explanation.surface: A comedian improvises during a match with a quick joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses the quip, which suits a down light read upwards; RU for rugby union is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something hastily, as in running up a dress or a curtain on the machine.

clue.text: Sneer at models from the Orient

indicators.note: models as a verb means the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone mocks fashion models from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like the object of 'Sneer at', but it is the verb shaping SNEER AT anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the East, especially Asia, as the Orient is the old name for the eastern world.

clue.text: At some distance switches failed

indicators.note: switches as a verb means the letters of the next word swap places

explanation.surface: A remote report that the switches have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' looks like the subject of 'failed', but it is the anagram signal working on FAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away from home or base is exactly the sense of the adverb, as in roaming far afield.

clue.text: A soldier without military personnel transport

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for soldier wraps round the letters for military personnel

parts.note: a fighter is a soldier
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army personnel

explanation.surface: A soldier goes about with no military staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but in its older sense it means outside, so the soldier surrounds the Royal Engineers rather than doing without them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo ship or aircraft is a means of carrying goods.

clue.text: Cheer for England towards the end

parts.note: late means near the end, as in late in the day

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers for England as the match nears its close.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift the spirits, to make someone happy, as a verb.

clue.text: The' weight-watcher is put off consuming one

indicators.note: consuming means the word for put off swallows the numeral for one

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slimmer is put off eating anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts I inside DETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a slimming regime counts calories to keep weight down.

clue.text: Run to raise money and totter

indicators.note: in a down answer raising the money letter puts it on top of the rest

parts.note: L is the pound sign, from Latin librae, money
one who tots up figures is an adder

explanation.surface: A charity fun run to raise money that leaves someone staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totter' looks like stagger; it is one who tots, that is adds up. 'to raise' puts L at the top of a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in stockings or tights is a vertical line of laddered stitches.

clue.text: Clear this tract of country

definitions.meaning: a wide stretch of flat land

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious means plain as an adjective; a broad level expanse of land is a plain as a noun.

clue.text: Draw the old fellow

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a friend or fellow

explanation.surface: Someone sketching an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching; it is the noun, a game ending level, here in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a position where the side to move has no legal move ends the game as a tie.

clue.text: Extended alfresco meal

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, out
a spread is a lavish meal laid out

explanation.surface: A long open-air picnic that goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretched or spread wide open is the sense, as in arms flung out.

clue.text: Not all blackleg rebels get the bird

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Strike-breakers and rebels are booed off, getting the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' is the idiom for being booed or jeered; here it is a plain instruction to find a bird. A blackleg is a strike-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird of lakes and rivers, the great crested one being well known in Britain.

clue.text: Many skirt the issue, but blush

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword's many
to skirt is to go round the edge, a rim
a son is a child, one's issue

explanation.surface: A crowd dodges the question but goes red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt the issue' reads as evading a question, but skirt and issue are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To go a deep red in the face, as a verb, is to flush or redden like the colour.

clue.text: Building material's sent, and so tipped out

indicators.note: tipped out means the letters are spilled and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A load of building stone is delivered and dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped out' suits a lorry load, but it rearranges SENT AND SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary rock quarried for building is used for walls and houses.

clue.text: Going around putting rubbish by a railway

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dumping garbage beside the railway line on their rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning on an axis or circling is the sense of a rotary engine or motion.

clue.text: Give changed order to back and a row will follow

indicators.note: will follow says the words for a row come after the word for back

parts.note: rear is the back
a range is a row, as a range of hills

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant reorders the ranks from the back, a row following.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a new sequence or layout, to reorganise.

clue.text: The result of athletes doing their level best

definitions.text: The result of athletes doing their level best

parts.words: The result of athletes doing their level best
parts.note: doing their level best reads as trying hard, but level means finishing exactly together

explanation.definitionFit: A race where two runners cross the line together ends in a tie.

clue.text: Making a note to complete a business programme

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
to end is to complete or finish

explanation.surface: Writing a memo to round off a firm's schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is only a link here; 'to complete' gives END, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is the running order of the session.

clue.text: She could well be astir before many

indicators.note: could well be says the letters of astir might easily form another word

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword's many

explanation.surface: A woman who might be up and about before most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could well be' signals rearranging the word astir, giving ASTRI; 'before many' then puts D, Roman 500, after it. Astrid is a Scandinavian name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian girl's name, so a woman, referred to as she.

clue.text: Hit back and grab share

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in reverse order

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow or hit
to take is to grab or seize

explanation.surface: A violent thief strikes back and seizes a cut of the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals reading the word for hit backwards, giving PAR; the surface's 'hit back' as retaliation is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a portion of something, especially food or an activity, is to join in or take part.

clue.text: With coppers about, are apt to put on an act

parts.note: P stands for pence, coins once of copper
re means about or concerning
to tend is to be apt or inclined to

explanation.surface: When police are around, people tend to pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; it means pennies, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To fake or feign, to make believe as an actor does.

clue.text: Display of bad spirit over work can cause strike

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
an act is a deed or work

explanation.surface: A show of bad temper about the job may lead to industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout, but here it is a collision, a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The force of one body hitting another is a collision or blow.

clue.text: Posts for sound men

indicators.note: sound here signals that the word for men is spoken and heard, not written

parts.note: males are men

explanation.surface: Jobs going for strong-voiced men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound men' suggests reliable men; 'sound' is the signal that MALES is heard, giving the spelling for letters sent by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Sends by letter or parcel, as a verb: one posts or mails a package.

clue.text: Bring on popular non-pedigree dog

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a cur is a mongrel

explanation.surface: Send on a well-liked mongrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something unwelcome on oneself, such as debts or anger.

clue.text: Certain to step outside, which will be much appreciated

indicators.note: outside says the word for step goes round the word for certain

parts.note: a tread is a step, as on a staircase
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A promise that a stroll outdoors will be well received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' tells the step to go round the word for certain; 'to step outside' reads as going out of doors, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held dear and valued highly, like a prized possession.

clue.text: Surreptitiously move left within the party

indicators.note: within means the letter for left goes inside the word for party

parts.note: a side is a team or party

explanation.surface: A political defector creeps leftwards inside the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts L inside SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge furtively, to creep sideways so as not to attract notice.

clue.text: A reclusive person taking tea — no rich spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hermit makes do with tea, no rich spread on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like food on the table, but it rearranges TEA and NO RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit who withdraws from the world for religious reasons is a classic recluse.

clue.text: Close English studies first

indicators.note: first says the word for studies comes before the abbreviation for English

parts.note: dens are studies, private rooms for work

explanation.surface: Someone shuts the English books before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb; it is the adjective meaning thick or packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick and tightly packed, as close or dense fog.

clue.text: The 16 painter

definitions.meaning: 16 across means going around, so one that goes round, or a lathe worker who shapes on a spinning wheel
J M W ..., the English landscape artist

explanation.surface: Naming the painter of something rotary.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 16 across, ROTARY; the answer is one who turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rotates or a lathe operator is one who spins things; the great romantic landscape artist bears the same surname.

clue.text: Admirer finds the lady in a depression

indicators.note: in places the word for the lady inside the words for a depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
her refers to a woman, the lady

explanation.surface: A fan discovers a woman down in a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the lady inside the hollow, splitting A and DENT around her; 'finds' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or person, a devoted fan.
